newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWF Australia sorghum forecast fairly steady.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWF Australia sorghum forecast fairly steady.

text.p: Australian Wheat Forecasters Pty Ltd has lifted slightly its forecast for Australian sorghum production in 1997 to 1.14 million tonnes from 1.11 million tonnes in its February forecast.
However, production was still seen lower than the 1.53 million tonnes produced in 1996.
AWF said continuing rain over the Australian grain sorghum growing areas had delayed the harvest without increasing yields in most areas.
It said there had been some trade short positions caused by the wet weather, causing the domestic sorghum market to firm for nearby positions.
As well, growers had been holding freshly harvest grain and this had further reduced supply, causing price rises in the sorghum markets of the eastern states.
AWF said the harvest in both New South Wales and southern Queensland should be complete by mid-April, presuming there is a return to dry conditions over th next month.
Central Queensland had been awaiting suitable soil condtions to sow sorghum since mid-January.
Those growers who waited now had soils still too wet to work, and the window of opportunity for sorghum sowing was closing.
"At this late stage in the summer cropping programme, sunflower seed has more appeal," AWF said.
Sorghum sown in central Queensland over the next two weeks would not be harvested until July/August.
